body:
# Independent audit of finite-base attained-counterexample compactification

Audited files:

- `candidate c280bb0dcfd30f3d`;
- `candidate dbf3b23d25004153`;
- the cone-volume and maximal-simplex lemmas in
  `candidate 2a5bf571e6159901`.

The reduction passes this audit for d>=1 and actual positive families on
the finite specified bases used in the statement. It transfers a strict
counterexample to the stronger gamma_d/h(P) target to an attained positive
one on a canonical minor. It does not prove that target or OC.

## 1. Dependence components and Helly numbers

For a nonvertex z, its minimal face contains all sources of any anchored
convex representation. Conversely z is in the relative interior of the
convex hull of the other points of that face, since these include all face
vertices. Giving each source a sufficiently small positive coefficient and
representing the residual point proves the required positive representation.
Thus the hyperedge and anchored-representation definitions of components
coincide, including isolated vertices.

Closure splits exactly over these components. A representation using its
target as one source can have that coefficient removed unless it is one;
the latter case is immediate. This proves that every component is closed.
The Helly upper bound is a union of componentwise infeasible certificates.
For the lower bound, extending a minimal infeasible trace from one component
by all other components is a closed trace, and removal of one such trace
retains its original component witness. The sum formula is exact.

If T is closed in U, every T-closed trace is U-closed: its convex hull lies
in conv(T), whose U-trace is T. Therefore the same minimal infeasible trace
families show h(T)<=h(U). No monotonicity for arbitrary nonclosed subsets
is being used.

## 2. Canonical lift and finite minor closure

Original affine coordinates belong to L(U), so the lift is injective and
has an affine projection back to U. An anchored representation lifts by
definition and projects back conversely. Thus closed traces and Helly
numbers are exactly preserved. The chosen basis spans every representation-
preserving function, yielding L(Phi(U))=Aff(Phi(U)).

A closed subset of Phi(U) corresponds to a closed subset T of U. If U was
P-closed, then P intersect conv(T) is contained in U and hence equals T.
Taking another universal lift gives the same anchored representation system
as Phi(T), so the resulting sets are affinely equivalent. This verifies
closure of the finite canonical-minor list, including component minors.

## 3. Minimality and positive limiting masses

Depth decreases or stays unchanged under canonical lifting, because every
original halfspace pulls back and the map is a volume-preserving translation
on each continuous fiber. A pullback which is the whole lifted affine hull
has mass one and does not affect the inequality.

Discarding fibers gives the correct inequality

    D_U >= (M_T/M_U) D_(T in U).

Hence a maximal mass-to-Helly component of a bad family is a strictly bad
smaller canonical minor. This establishes connectedness of the chosen
minimal bad base.

Along a unit-mass sequence the positive limiting mass support T is closed:
one positive source in a fixed convex representation supplies a translated
positive multiple of its body inside the target. No convergence of shapes
or positions is needed. If T is proper, its retained mass tends to one and
the preceding depth inequalities give b_d(Phi(T))<=beta. Since the threshold
gamma_d/h(T) is at least gamma_d/h(U), this contradicts minimality. Thus
every limiting mass is positive, and there is a common positive lower bound
along the selected subsequence.

## 4. Shape propagation and removal of position drift

The cone-volume lemma is valid in every d>=1: a bounded positive-volume
subset has a section with area approaching at least v/(2R), and the cone
from that section to an arbitrary distant target point has volume at least
(T-R)v/(2dR). Its containing-body volume bound controls the point's distance.

In a fixed positive anchored representation, a bounded source gives a
bounded translated positive-volume subset of the target. The cone lemma
bounds the target diameter. Its containment of translated multiples of all
other sources then bounds their diameters. The stated loose propagation
factor works over a spanning traversal of each finite component. A maximal
inscribed simplex supplies the determinant-one bounded anchor, with its
maximum attained by compactness. Singleton components need no propagation.

Centroid errors for each representation row are bounded by the common
diameter because both the target centroid and the combination of source
centroids belong to the target body. A finite row matrix can be taken from
vertices of the anchored-representation polytopes. Orthogonal projection
onto its kernel gives the stated finite residual bound. On the universal
lift this kernel consists of ordinary affine functions, so subtracting the
projected vector array is one ambient affine shear. Halfspaces and all fiber
volumes are preserved. No nonlinear independent translation is substituted
for that shear.

## 5. Limits and maximum depth

Simultaneous bounded Hausdorff convergence preserves every compatibility
inclusion by approximating source points with the coefficients fixed.
Finite convex-body indicator functions converge in L1, including degenerate
limits, and the positive mass lower bound keeps all final fibers positive.

For candidate movement in one fiber, normalize the continuous cap normal
to length one and use the enclosing ball's maximal (d-1)-section area to
bound the intervening slab. The integer coefficients can be arbitrarily
large without changing this estimate. Pure base cuts do not change at all.
Taking infima, then using total variation convergence and compact candidate
fibers, proves convergence of maximum depth in both directions. Closed
vertical boundaries, nonunique maximizing candidates, and oblique cuts
are all covered.

## 6. Bounded canonical-hull facet class

Inscribed finite nets at all specified fibers give a polytope whose actual
fibers lie between each net hull and its original body. Hence the actual
fibers converge individually and strict badness persists. The hull is full
dimensional relative to aff(B) times R^d because B spans its affine hull
and the continuous fibers are positive.

Fixing its finite facet budget produces a nonempty strict-bad class. A
minimizing sequence in that class still cannot lose a fiber: a lost-fiber
subsequence would produce a smaller bad canonical minor in the UNRESTRICTED
class, contradicting the earlier choice of B. The restriction or lift need
not preserve the facet budget for this contradiction. This distinction is
correct in the source.

Affine normalization preserves the canonical hull's facet count. Its limit
has interior; normalize each facet normal and take bounded offsets. A ball
strictly inside the limiting hull supplies strict feasibility. Contracting
an arbitrary point of the limiting inequality system toward that ball
center proves equality of that system with the Hausdorff limit. Thus the
limit still has at most N facets. This is a canonical-hull facet statement;
it is distinct from a shared-N representable-plane class and does not prove
that the unrestricted infimum is attained by a polytope.

Finally dim aff(B)=dim L(U)-1<=h(B)-1: facets of an affine simplex with
vertices in B give a minimal infeasible family of size dim aff(B)+1.
